recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis).
recording.note: Commons describes first release in 1930; the Public Domain Project identifies Electrola EJ 423, order 6-0755, matrix CVE-48936, and tentatively dates first release to 1930. The 1929 session-day disagreement does not affect the pre-1963 release bound. The source’s worldwide expiry claim and its website’s CC BY-SA notice are not used as a sound-recording licence. Usable under the programme’s pre-1963 European sound-recording rule; the former 50-year term had expired before the 2013 extension. This is territorial, not a worldwide licence; US sound-recording status is not established. A recording date alone is not represented as an independently verified first-publication date.

alternatives.value: Public-domain recording worldwide — claim made by the Public Domain Project and reproduced by Commons.
US pre-1972 sound-recording law provides a continuing term for a 1929/1930 first publication; no separate US permission is established.
